structure.title: Preface – July 26, 1771 · Letters from the country
structure.text: Werther writes to Wilhelm about drawing, children and the pleasures of an unhurried day. He meets Lotte cutting bread for her younger siblings. The sight feels like the fulfilment of something he has wanted long before he knew her.

structure.title: July 30, 1771 – December 6, 1772 · An engagement and an absence
structure.text: Lotte's fiancé Albert proves a particularly awkward obstacle because Werther likes him. Employment elsewhere offers Werther a different future. There too questions of rank and admission to company give him reasons to feel the world has made too little room for him.

structure.title: The Editor to the Reader · The editor takes over
structure.text: As the letters cease to give a continuous account, an editor pieces together testimony, papers and remembered conversations. For the first time other people's accounts can stand beside the feelings that have occupied almost every page.

people.name: Werther and Wilhelm
people.text: We read the writer's answers without the letters that provoked them. When Werther rebukes a sensible suggestion, his friend's entire case must be reconstructed from the words of the person who finds it unbearable.

people.name: Lotte
people.role: Daughter with a household to manage
people.text: Caring for her siblings gives Lotte daily obligations the visitor can admire and then leave behind. Her kindness toward Werther has to fit among loyalties that existed before he appeared at the door.

context.title: Books for a particular mood
context.text: Homer accompanies Werther in his early delight in ordinary things. The later attraction of Ossian brings a landscape of lost warriors, lament and dark weather. Changes on his bookshelf allow the same countryside to acquire a very different emotional scale.

notice.why: Cutting bread, keeping children in order or paying a visit occupies her for reasons quite apart from Werther. The intensity with which he sees her can make those independent purposes momentarily disappear.

notice.text: Compare returns to a favourite place.
notice.why: A village, a grove or a domestic scene can seem to have changed beyond recognition. Read the earlier letter beside the later one and it becomes difficult to say how much of the transformation belongs to the landscape.

opening: Werther meets a woman looking after her younger siblings and falls in love with the whole scene. Lotte is warm, intelligent, and already promised to someone else. Knowing that does very little to change what he feels, and his letters turn every meeting into evidence that this attachment has become the centre of his life. Goethe makes the intensity seductive enough to inhabit, while allowing the reader to see how a person can gradually organise an entire world around a desire it cannot satisfy.
